title: Performance antipatterns: chatty I/O, extraneous fetching, the busy database

videos.script: Some slow systems are slow because of a hard problem. Most are slow because of a small number of habits, repeated in thousands of places. {{habits}} They have names, and Microsoft's architecture guidance keeps a catalogue of them, the performance antipatterns. {{catalogue}} What they have in common is that they work perfectly on a developer's laptop, where the database is on the same machine and has ten rows. {{laptop}} On your machine you will put a millisecond of network between the shop and its database, which is about what separates two availability zones, and the habits become visible. {{latency}} A page that asks the database once per order instead of once. A catalogue that brings back a megabyte to show fifty names. {{n1}} And a front page that asks the database the same question for every visitor, a hundred times a minute, when the answer changes once an hour. {{busy}} Each fix is a few lines. Finding them is the skill, and the lesson ends with how.
